before: A first footnote or endnote in a file without a settings part created word/settings.xml, with its relationship and content type, only to list the new notes part's separators. Two people who added a first note at once in a Yjs room each created that part. Shared state kept one settings root, moved the other root's separator references into the notes part, and left a relationship that could point at no part, so every participant stopped applying changes.
after: The separator list is written into a settings part the file already has. A file without settings keeps none, and a first note writes only its notes part, its relationship, and its content type, as before the list was added.
reason: The edit writes fewer parts, and every part it still writes is one the journal already carried. No stored field, operation kind, or identity rule changes.
